title: Sustainable land management and restoration
provider: FAO elearning Academy (Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations), in partnership with CIHEAM-Bari, WOCAT, the Economics of Land Degradation (ELD) initiative, and University of Leeds
language: English and Arabic for this specific course. The FAO elearning Academy overall is multilingual (English, French, Spanish, Arabic and others). No Russian version of this course confirmed. [UNVERIFIED whether a Russian localization exists]
cost: Free of charge. All FAO elearning Academy courses (incl. the final certification test and digital badge) are provided at no cost as a "global public good." Self-registration on elearning.fao.org required.
certificate: Free verifiable digital badge / certificate of completion. Issued by FAO after passing the final scenario-based performance assessment with a score of 75% or higher. Badges conform to the Open Badges standard with embedded metadata (issuer, criteria, recipient, competency) and are externally verifiable via Badgecheck.io; shareable on LinkedIn / email signature / personal site. [UNVERIFIED that this exact course uses the badge test rather than a plain completion certificate — stated as the Academy-wide standard policy]
duration: Approximately 2 to 3.5 hours total, self-paced. The FAO course page lists ~3h30m across 5 lessons (each ~35–50 min); FAO's agroecology description cites it as a "2 hours long course." Released March 2019.
level: Introductory / general audience — written for non-specialists; no prior expertise required.
target_audience: Local and national policy makers; land and water management technicians; extension agents and agronomists; farmers and land users. Aimed at those involved in selecting, planning, implementing and monitoring SLM interventions and the enabling environment, framed around SDG target 15.3 (land degradation neutrality).

syllabus.module: Lesson 1 — Introduction to Sustainable Land Management and land restoration: basic principles
syllabus.topics: Core SLM and land restoration concepts; land degradation drivers; the case for SLM; SDG target 15.3 / land degradation neutrality framing. (~35–50 min)

syllabus.module: Lesson 2 — Planning implementation of SLM interventions
syllabus.topics: Participatory SLM land-use planning approach; selecting appropriate interventions; engaging stakeholders and land users. (~35–50 min)

syllabus.module: Lesson 3 — Tools of implementation of sustainable land management
syllabus.topics: Tools and methods for putting SLM into practice, including the WOCAT global network of SLM technologies and approaches. (~35–50 min)

syllabus.module: Lesson 4 — Incentives for transition to SLM
syllabus.topics: Enabling environment and economic incentives; the Economics of Land Degradation (ELD) initiative; cost-benefit reasoning for adopting SLM. (~35–50 min)
Monitoring and evaluating SLM outcomes; indicators of success; case study (e.g. Zambia) applying the approach. (~35–50 min)

format: Self-paced online e-learning on a Moodle-based platform; 5 interactive multimedia lessons with video, narrated content and embedded knowledge checks. Open-enrollment, no cohort/deadlines.
assessment: Embedded in-lesson knowledge checks plus a final certification test. Per FAO Academy policy the final assessment is scenario-based / performance-oriented and requires ≥75% to earn the certificate and digital badge. A course evaluation form is also offered. [UNVERIFIED that the 75% scenario-test applies to this specific course vs. a generic completion certificate]
hands_on: No software lab or coding. "Hands-on" is conceptual: a participatory SLM land-use planning walkthrough, real case studies (Zambia), and demonstrations of decision-support tools (WOCAT, ELD). It points learners to external tools rather than having them operate GIS/data tools inside the course. [Related FAO/GEF CACILM II trainings separately taught QGIS + the WOCAT watershed tool, but that is not part of course id=454.]
tools: WOCAT global SLM database/network; Economics of Land Degradation (ELD) initiative methodology; FAO participatory land-use planning approach. No proprietary software required to take the course.
strengths: Genuinely free, certified, and openly self-enrollable — strong fit with a $0-cost platform philosophy.
Tight, logical 5-lesson arc that mirrors the SLM project lifecycle: principles -> planning -> implementation tools -> incentives -> monitoring. Very reusable as a module skeleton.
Verifiable Open Badges credential with a clear, transparent 75% threshold and external verification (Badgecheck.io) — credible, copyable certification model.
Grounds content in recognized real tools (WOCAT, ELD) and concrete case studies rather than abstractions.
Explicitly multi-audience (policy makers -> technicians -> farmers), with non-specialist language that lowers the barrier for SMB practitioners.
Anchored to a recognized policy frame (SDG 15.3 / land degradation neutrality), giving the curriculum external legitimacy.
weaknesses: Short and high-level (~2–3.5h, introductory) — gives breadth, not the operational depth an SMB agronomist needs to actually execute SLM on a specific field.
No Russian version confirmed and not localized to Kazakhstan/Central Asia — cases (e.g. Zambia) are not regionally relevant to СКО/Костанай/Акмола.
No real hands-on tooling inside the course (no QGIS/GEE/data exercises); it references tools instead of training their use.
Available in only English + Arabic for this course, limiting direct reuse for a Russian-speaking audience.
Assessment is single final test rather than per-lesson graded practice; limited formative feedback.
Released 2019 — some material may predate newer datasets/methods.
borrow_for_folur: Copy the 5-lesson lifecycle backbone (принципы -> планирование -> инструменты внедрения -> стимулы/экономика -> мониторинг) as the canonical structure for FOLUR SLM modules — it is clean and audience-tested.

Adopt the Open Badges certification model: a verifiable digital badge with a transparent fixed threshold (FAO uses 75%). The FOLUR platform already has a stdlib certificate engine — align its pass threshold and add Open Badges-style embedded metadata + an external verification path (mirror Badgecheck.io with a GitHub Pages verify page).

Borrow the scenario-based / performance final assessment idea (decision scenarios) instead of pure multiple-choice — better for adult SMB practitioners; the existing test-engine variant generation can support this.
Replicate the explicit multi-audience layering (policy maker / technician / agronom / фермер) but re-cut it for North-Kazakhstan SMB, replacing the Zambia case with СКО/Костанай/Акмола cases.
Reuse the WOCAT + ELD framing: embed WOCAT SLM technologies and the ELD economics-of-degradation cost-benefit logic, localized with regional figures, as a credible open-data tool layer.
Imitate the 'global public good / fully free, no-admin enrollment' positioning — it validates the platform's $0, open-access invariant and can be cited as a peer benchmark.
Anchor FOLUR modules to SDG 15.3 / land-degradation-neutrality (as FAO does) to give the Russian-language curriculum recognized international legitimacy.

Where FAO is weak (no real GIS lab), differentiate FOLUR by adding the hands-on Colab/QGIS/GEE notebooks FAO omits — use FAO for the conceptual scaffolding, then go deeper with regional, runnable, open-data exercises.
